Person (Musician).label: Person
Person (Musician).comment: A Person is an individual human being, whether alive, dead, undead, or fictional. Also called individual, human, character. Examples: John Doe, Albert Einstein, Sherlock Holmes. Distinct from Organization, which is a group of people.

Person (Musician).label: MusicEvent
Person (Musician).comment: A MusicEvent is an event primarily featuring musical performances. Also called concert, musical performance, gig. Examples: a rock concert, a classical symphony performance, a music festival. Distinct from PerformingArtsEvent, which includes broader performance types like theatre or dance.

Person (Musician).label: MusicGroup
Person (Musician).comment: A MusicGroup, as a PerformingGroup, is an organization of musicians, such as a band or orchestra, or a solo musician. Also called band, musical ensemble, orchestra, solo artist. Examples: The Beatles, New York Philharmonic, Taylor Swift. Distinct from PerformingGroup, which is a broader category for any performance group.

Person (Musician).label: PeopleAudience
Person (Musician).comment: A PeopleAudience, as an Audience, describes a set of characteristics belonging to people, e.g., who compose an item's target audience. Also called demographic group, target audience, human audience. Examples: 'adults aged 18-35', 'students', 'retirees'. Distinct from Audience, which is a broader category including non-human audiences.

Person (Musician).label: MusicAlbum
Person (Musician).comment: A MusicAlbum, as a MusicPlaylist, is a collection of music tracks released together. Also called album, record album, studio album. Examples: 'Thriller' by Michael Jackson, 'Abbey Road' by The Beatles, a compilation album. Distinct from MusicRecording, which is usually a single song.

Person (American Football Player).label: Person
Person (American Football Player).comment: A Person is an individual human being, whether alive, dead, undead, or fictional. Also called individual, human, character. Examples: John Doe, Albert Einstein, Sherlock Holmes. Distinct from Organization, which is a group of people.

Person (American Football Player).label: SportsActivityLocation
Person (American Football Player).comment: A local business or facility providing a venue for sports activities. Also called sports venue, athletic facility, recreation center, playing field. Examples: a local gym, a public tennis court, a community swimming pool, a golf course.

Person (American Football Player).label: SportsEvent
Person (American Football Player).comment: An event involving athletic competition or display. Also called athletic contest, game, match, sporting competition. Examples: a football game, an Olympic event, a marathon race, a tennis tournament.

Person (American Football Player).label: SportsTeam
Person (American Football Player).comment: An organization consisting of a group of athletes who compete together in a sport. Also called athletic team, squad, club, side. Examples: the Los Angeles Lakers, the New England Patriots, a high school basketball team.

Person (American Football Player).label: SportsOrganization
Person (American Football Player).comment: A general category for organizations involved in sports, including teams, governing bodies, and associations. Also called athletic organization, sports body, sports group. Examples: the NBA, a local youth soccer league, the International Olympic Committee.

Venue (Arena).label: StadiumOrArena
Venue (Arena).comment: A large civic structure designed for sporting events, concerts, or other large-scale public gatherings. Also called stadium, arena, coliseum, sports complex. Examples: Wembley Stadium, Madison Square Garden, the Roman Colosseum.

Venue (Arena).label: SportsActivityLocation
Venue (Arena).comment: A local business or facility providing a venue for sports activities. Also called sports venue, athletic facility, recreation center, playing field. Examples: a local gym, a public tennis court, a community swimming pool, a golf course.

Venue (Arena).label: EventVenue
Venue (Arena).comment: An EventVenue is a CivicStructure that serves as a location for events. Also called venue, event space, performance hall. Examples: A concert hall, a stadium, a conference center, a community hall.

Venue (Arena).label: SportsEvent
Venue (Arena).comment: An event involving athletic competition or display. Also called athletic contest, game, match, sporting competition. Examples: a football game, an Olympic event, a marathon race, a tennis tournament.

Venue (Arena).label: Place
Venue (Arena).comment: A Place is an entity that has a somewhat fixed, physical extension. Also called location, venue, site. Examples: a city, a building, a park, a specific address. Distinct from Event, which is a happening in time.

City.label: City
City.comment: A large and permanent human settlement, typically an administrative area with a defined government. Also called town, municipality, urban area, metropolis. Examples: New York City, London, Tokyo, Paris. Distinct from AdministrativeArea, which is a broader category including states, provinces, etc.

City.label: Residence
City.comment: A Residence is a Place where a person lives. Also called home, dwelling, abode. Examples: a house, an apartment, a condominium, a dormitory room.

City.label: Place
City.comment: A Place is an entity that has a somewhat fixed, physical extension. Also called location, venue, site. Examples: a city, a building, a park, a specific address. Distinct from Event, which is a happening in time.

City.label: StadiumOrArena
City.comment: A large civic structure designed for sporting events, concerts, or other large-scale public gatherings. Also called stadium, arena, coliseum, sports complex. Examples: Wembley Stadium, Madison Square Garden, the Roman Colosseum.

City.label: House
City.comment: A House is an accommodation type representing a building or structure intended for human or other creature habitation. Also called dwelling, residence, home. Examples: a single-family home, a townhouse, a cottage. Distinct from Apartment, which is a unit within a larger building, and HotelRoom, which is a temporary lodging unit.

Person (Actress).label: Person
Person (Actress).comment: A Person is an individual human being, whether alive, dead, undead, or fictional. Also called individual, human, character. Examples: John Doe, Albert Einstein, Sherlock Holmes. Distinct from Organization, which is a group of people.

Person (Actress).label: PerformanceRole
Person (Actress).comment: A PerformanceRole, as a Role, is a role an entity plays in a theatrical performance, such as a movie or TV series. Also called acting role, character role, stage role. Examples: 'actor in a film', 'director of a play', 'musician in a concert'. Distinct from OrganizationRole, which is a role within an organization.

Person (Actress).label: Play
Person (Actress).comment: A Play is a CreativeWork in the form of literature, primarily consisting of dialogue between characters, intended for theatrical performance. Also called stage play, drama, theatrical work. Examples: "Hamlet", "Death of a Salesman", "Hamilton", "A Streetcar Named Desire". Distinct from TheaterEvent, which is the actual performance of a play.

Person (Actress).label: TheaterEvent
Person (Actress).comment: An event representing a live performance in a theater. Also called stage play, theatrical show, drama performance. Examples: a Broadway musical, a local community play, a Shakespearean tragedy.

Person (Actress).label: TheaterGroup
Person (Actress).comment: An organization or company dedicated to producing and performing theatrical works. Also called theater company, drama troupe, acting ensemble. Examples: The Royal Shakespeare Company, Cirque du Soleil, a local amateur dramatics society.

Person (Music Producer).label: Person
Person (Music Producer).comment: A Person is an individual human being, whether alive, dead, undead, or fictional. Also called individual, human, character. Examples: John Doe, Albert Einstein, Sherlock Holmes. Distinct from Organization, which is a group of people.

Person (Music Producer).label: MusicRecording
Person (Music Producer).comment: A MusicRecording, as a CreativeWork, is a recorded performance of a musical composition, usually a single song. Also called music track, song recording, audio track. Examples: 'Yesterday' by The Beatles (the recorded version), a single from an album, a demo track. Distinct from MusicComposition, which is the abstract musical work.

Person (Music Producer).label: MusicAlbumProductionType
Person (Music Producer).comment: MusicAlbumProductionType is an enumeration classifying a music album by its content type. Also called album type, production category. Examples: StudioAlbum, LiveAlbum, Soundtrack, CompilationAlbum. Distinct from MusicAlbumReleaseType, which describes the release format.

Person (Music Producer).label: MusicAlbum
Person (Music Producer).comment: A MusicAlbum, as a MusicPlaylist, is a collection of music tracks released together. Also called album, record album, studio album. Examples: 'Thriller' by Michael Jackson, 'Abbey Road' by The Beatles, a compilation album. Distinct from MusicRecording, which is usually a single song.

Person (Music Producer).label: MusicEvent
Person (Music Producer).comment: A MusicEvent is an event primarily featuring musical performances. Also called concert, musical performance, gig. Examples: a rock concert, a classical symphony performance, a music festival. Distinct from PerformingArtsEvent, which includes broader performance types like theatre or dance.

Time of Day.label: Time
Time of Day.comment: A data type representing a specific point in time, typically in hh:mm:ss format, potentially with a timezone offset. Also called timestamp, clock time, time of day. Examples: "14:30:00", "09:00:00Z", "17:45:30+01:00".

Time of Day.label: DateTime
Time of Day.comment: A data type representing a specific point in time, combining both date and time components according to ISO 8601. Also called Timestamp, date and time string, ISO 8601 datetime. Examples: "2023-10-27T10:30:00Z", "1999-12-31T23:59:59-05:00", "2024-01-15T14:00:00". Distinct from Date, which only specifies a calendar date without time.

Time of Day.label: Duration
Time of Day.comment: As a Quantity, Duration represents a period of time, typically expressed in ISO 8601 format. Also called time span, period, length of time. Examples: "PT1H30M" (1 hour 30 minutes), "P3D" (3 days), "PT2H" (2 hours).

Time of Day.label: Date
Time of Day.comment: Date is a data type representing a specific calendar date, typically formatted according to ISO 8601. Also called calendar date, specific day. Examples: "2023-10-27", "1999-12-31", "0001-01-01".

Time of Day.label: DayOfWeek
Time of Day.comment: An enumeration representing a specific day of the week, used for scheduling or recurring events. Also called Weekday, calendar day, day name. Examples: Monday, Tuesday, Saturday, Sunday. Distinct from Date, which specifies a particular calendar date.

Day of Week.label: DayOfWeek
Day of Week.comment: An enumeration representing a specific day of the week, used for scheduling or recurring events. Also called Weekday, calendar day, day name. Examples: Monday, Tuesday, Saturday, Sunday. Distinct from Date, which specifies a particular calendar date.

Day of Week.label: Schedule
Day of Week.comment: A definition of a repeating time period used to describe a regularly occurring event, specifying frequency, days, and start/end times. Also called timetable, recurring event plan, calendar entry, routine. Examples: a weekly yoga class schedule, a bus route timetable, a daily meeting schedule, a concert series calendar.

Day of Week.label: Date
Day of Week.comment: Date is a data type representing a specific calendar date, typically formatted according to ISO 8601. Also called calendar date, specific day. Examples: "2023-10-27", "1999-12-31", "0001-01-01".

Day of Week.label: Time
Day of Week.comment: A data type representing a specific point in time, typically in hh:mm:ss format, potentially with a timezone offset. Also called timestamp, clock time, time of day. Examples: "14:30:00", "09:00:00Z", "17:45:30+01:00".

Day of Week.label: TVSeason
Day of Week.comment: A distinct period of a television series, comprising multiple episodes, dedicated to TV broadcast and associated online delivery. Also called television season, broadcast season, show season. Examples: 'Season 1 of The Crown', 'The final season of Breaking Bad'. Distinct from Season, which is a more general media season.

Media Outlet.label: NewsMediaOrganization
Media Outlet.comment: A NewsMediaOrganization is an organization that produces and disseminates news, such as a newspaper or TV station. Also called news agency, media outlet, journalistic organization. Examples: The New York Times, BBC News, CNN. Distinct from Organization, which is a broader category for any type of organization.

Media Outlet.label: TelevisionStation
Media Outlet.comment: A local business or organization that broadcasts television programs. Also called TV broadcaster, broadcast station, local TV channel. Examples: 'WNBC (New York)', 'BBC Television Centre', a local news station.

Media Outlet.label: BroadcastEvent
Media Outlet.comment: A BroadcastEvent is a PublicationEvent representing an event that is transmitted over the air or online. Also called live broadcast, streamed event, televised event, radio broadcast. Examples: a live news report, a sports game broadcast, a concert livestream.

Media Outlet.label: NewsArticle
Media Outlet.comment: A NewsArticle, as an Article, is a creative work whose content reports news or provides background context for understanding news. Also called news report, news story, journalistic article. Examples: a breaking news report, an investigative journalism piece, an opinion column in a newspaper. Distinct from BlogPosting, which is typically less formal and often personal.

Media Outlet.label: BroadcastService
Media Outlet.comment: A BroadcastService is a Service that delivers content via broadcast, either over the air or online. Also called broadcasting service, media transmission service, content delivery service. Examples: a national television network, a satellite radio provider, an internet radio service.

Date Range.label: Date
Date Range.comment: Date is a data type representing a specific calendar date, typically formatted according to ISO 8601. Also called calendar date, specific day. Examples: "2023-10-27", "1999-12-31", "0001-01-01".

Date Range.label: ServicePeriod
Date Range.comment: A structured value representing a duration for a service, often including constraints like cutoff times or business days. Also called service duration, operational window, delivery timeframe, handling period. Examples: a 2-day shipping period with a 3 PM cutoff, a 5-business-day processing time, a 24/7 support period.

Event (General).label: SocialEvent
Event (General).comment: An event primarily focused on social interaction and entertainment. Also called party, gathering, social function, get-together. Examples: a birthday party, a wedding reception, a community picnic, a networking mixer.

Event (General).label: Event
Event (General).comment: An Event is a Thing happening at a specific time and location, such as a concert, lecture, or festival. Also called happening, occurrence, occasion. Examples: A rock concert, a public lecture, a sports match, a community festival.

Event (General).label: ConferenceEvent
Event (General).comment: An event specifically organized as a conference, typically involving presentations, discussions, and networking. Also called conference, convention, symposium, summit. Examples: A tech conference, an academic symposium, a business summit, a medical convention. Distinct from Event, which is a general occurrence.

Event (General).label: SportsEvent
Event (General).comment: An event involving athletic competition or display. Also called athletic contest, game, match, sporting competition. Examples: a football game, an Olympic event, a marathon race, a tennis tournament.

Event (General).label: Festival
Event (General).comment: A Festival is an Event that is a public celebration or series of special events. Also called celebration, gala, fete. Examples: A music festival, a film festival, a cultural heritage festival, a food and wine festival.

Monetary Amount.label: MonetaryAmount
Monetary Amount.comment: A structured value representing a monetary value or range, typically expressed with a currency. Also called amount of money, financial value, currency amount. Examples: "$50 USD", "£1,000 to £1,000,000 GBP", "€25.99". Distinct from PriceSpecification, which describes the price of an offer.

Monetary Amount.label: MonetaryGrant
Monetary Amount.comment: An intangible grant that provides a sum of money. Also called financial grant, money award, cash donation. Examples: a research grant, a scholarship, a government subsidy. Distinct from Grant, which can be non-monetary.

Monetary Amount.label: Quantity
Monetary Amount.comment: Quantity is a data type representing measurable amounts such as distance, time, mass, or weight. Also called amount, measure, magnitude. Examples: '3 kg', '4 milligrams', '10 meters', '2 hours'.

Monetary Amount.label: DatedMoneySpecification
Monetary Amount.comment: A structured value representing a monetary amount that is valid or applicable over a specified time period, though its use is superseded by MonetaryAmount. Also called Time-bound monetary value, period-specific money, dated financial amount. Examples: An employee's salary from 2022-01-01 to 2022-12-31, a subscription fee valid for a quarter, a bonus paid for a specific fiscal year.

Monetary Amount.label: Mass
Monetary Amount.comment: A quantity representing the amount of matter in an object, typically expressed with a unit of measure. Also called weight, bulk, quantity of matter. Examples: "5 kg", "10 pounds", "200 grams", "1 ton". Distinct from Quantity, which is a broader concept for any measurable amount.

Country.label: Country
Country.comment: A Country is a sovereign state or nation, representing a primary administrative division of the Earth's surface. Also called nation, state, sovereign state, realm. Examples: United States, Canada, France, Japan, Brazil.

Country.label: State
Country.comment: A major administrative division of a country, such as a state or province. Also called province, region, territory, commonwealth. Examples: California, Ontario, Bavaria, Texas.

Country.label: DefenceEstablishment
Country.comment: A government building or civic structure primarily used for military or national defense purposes. Also called Military base, army base, naval base, air force station. Examples: The Pentagon, Fort Bragg, Pearl Harbor Naval Shipyard, Royal Air Force Lakenheath. Distinct from GovernmentBuilding, which is a broader category for any government facility.

Country.label: Continent
Country.comment: One of the Earth's large landmasses, such as Europe or Africa. Also called major landmass, global region, land continent. Examples: Asia, North America, Antarctica, Australia. Distinct from Landform, which is a general term for a natural feature of the Earth's surface.

Country.label: Place
Country.comment: A Place is an entity that has a somewhat fixed, physical extension. Also called location, venue, site. Examples: a city, a building, a park, a specific address. Distinct from Event, which is a happening in time.

Sports League.label: SportsTeam
Sports League.comment: An organization consisting of a group of athletes who compete together in a sport. Also called athletic team, squad, club, side. Examples: the Los Angeles Lakers, the New England Patriots, a high school basketball team.

Sports League.label: SportsOrganization
Sports League.comment: A general category for organizations involved in sports, including teams, governing bodies, and associations. Also called athletic organization, sports body, sports group. Examples: the NBA, a local youth soccer league, the International Olympic Committee.

Sports League.label: SportsEvent
Sports League.comment: An event involving athletic competition or display. Also called athletic contest, game, match, sporting competition. Examples: a football game, an Olympic event, a marathon race, a tennis tournament.

Sports League.label: SportsClub
Sports League.comment: A local business or organization dedicated to a specific sport or range of sports, often offering membership and facilities. Also called athletic club, sports association, fitness club. Examples: a local tennis club, a community soccer club, a professional golf club.

Sports League.label: SportsActivityLocation
Sports League.comment: A local business or facility providing a venue for sports activities. Also called sports venue, athletic facility, recreation center, playing field. Examples: a local gym, a public tennis court, a community swimming pool, a golf course.

Group of People (Representatives).label: PerformingGroup
Group of People (Representatives).comment: A PerformingGroup is an organization of performers, such as a band, orchestra, or circus. Also called performance ensemble, troupe, artistic group. Examples: Cirque du Soleil, a local theatre company, a dance troupe. Distinct from MusicGroup, which is specifically for musical performers.

Group of People (Representatives).label: Organization
Group of People (Representatives).comment: An Organization is a group of people with a particular purpose, such as a school, NGO, corporation, or club. Also called entity, institution, association. Examples: Google, Harvard University, Red Cross, a local sports club. Distinct from Person, which is an individual.

Group of People (Representatives).label: Cooperative
Group of People (Representatives).comment: A Cooperative is an organization formed as a joint project by multiple organizations or individuals, often for mutual benefit. Also called member-owned business, co-op, collective. Examples: REI (Recreational Equipment, Inc.), Ocean Spray, Sunkist Growers, credit unions. Distinct from Corporation, which is a business entity owned by shareholders.

Group of People (Representatives).label: TheaterGroup
Group of People (Representatives).comment: An organization or company dedicated to producing and performing theatrical works. Also called theater company, drama troupe, acting ensemble. Examples: The Royal Shakespeare Company, Cirque du Soleil, a local amateur dramatics society.

Group of People (Representatives).label: MusicGroup
Group of People (Representatives).comment: A MusicGroup, as a PerformingGroup, is an organization of musicians, such as a band or orchestra, or a solo musician. Also called band, musical ensemble, orchestra, solo artist. Examples: The Beatles, New York Philharmonic, Taylor Swift. Distinct from PerformingGroup, which is a broader category for any performance group.

News Agency.label: NewsMediaOrganization
News Agency.comment: A NewsMediaOrganization is an organization that produces and disseminates news, such as a newspaper or TV station. Also called news agency, media outlet, journalistic organization. Examples: The New York Times, BBC News, CNN. Distinct from Organization, which is a broader category for any type of organization.

News Agency.label: NewsArticle
News Agency.comment: A NewsArticle, as an Article, is a creative work whose content reports news or provides background context for understanding news. Also called news report, news story, journalistic article. Examples: a breaking news report, an investigative journalism piece, an opinion column in a newspaper. Distinct from BlogPosting, which is typically less formal and often personal.

News Agency.label: ReportageNewsArticle
News Agency.comment: A ReportageNewsArticle is a NewsArticle representing news articles based on factual journalistic reporting, emphasizing verified information and multiple viewpoints. Also called news report, journalistic article, factual news. Examples: a breaking news story about a political event, an investigative report on a social issue, a factual account of a natural disaster, a report on scientific findings. Distinct from AnalysisNewsArticle, which goes deeper into analysis.

News Agency.label: Report
News Agency.comment: A Report is an Article generated by a governmental or non-governmental organization. Also called official report, document, publication. Examples: an annual financial report, a government research report, a UN policy report, a company's sustainability report.

News Agency.label: TelevisionStation
News Agency.comment: A local business or organization that broadcasts television programs. Also called TV broadcaster, broadcast station, local TV channel. Examples: 'WNBC (New York)', 'BBC Television Centre', a local news station.

Event (Specific).label: Event

Event (Specific).label: ConferenceEvent
Event (Specific).comment: An event specifically organized as a conference, typically involving presentations, discussions, and networking. Also called conference, convention, symposium, summit. Examples: A tech conference, an academic symposium, a business summit, a medical convention. Distinct from Event, which is a general occurrence.

Event (Specific).label: DeliveryEvent
Event (Specific).comment: An event representing the delivery of an item, typically a product or package. Also called Shipping event, package delivery, consignment event. Examples: A package arriving at its destination, a food delivery being completed, a furniture delivery appointment. Distinct from Order, which is the request for items, not the delivery itself.

Event (Specific).label: SocialEvent
Event (Specific).comment: An event primarily focused on social interaction and entertainment. Also called party, gathering, social function, get-together. Examples: a birthday party, a wedding reception, a community picnic, a networking mixer.

Event (Specific).label: SportsEvent

Political Office Holder (Generic).label: PoliticalParty
Political Office Holder (Generic).comment: A PoliticalParty is an Organization formed to contest elections and hold power in government. Also called political movement, party. Examples: Democratic Party, Republican Party, Labour Party, Conservative Party.

Political Office Holder (Generic).label: Person
Political Office Holder (Generic).comment: A Person is an individual human being, whether alive, dead, undead, or fictional. Also called individual, human, character. Examples: John Doe, Albert Einstein, Sherlock Holmes. Distinct from Organization, which is a group of people.

Political Office Holder (Generic).label: GovernmentBenefitsType
Political Office Holder (Generic).comment: GovernmentBenefitsType is an enumeration of various government benefits, particularly those related to supporting situations like COVID-19. Also called public assistance types, state aid categories, welfare program kinds. Examples: unemployment benefits, stimulus checks, housing assistance, food stamps.

Political Office Holder (Generic).label: GovernmentOffice
Political Office Holder (Generic).comment: A GovernmentOffice is a local business representing a specific governmental agency or department. Also called public agency office, state department branch, municipal service center. Examples: IRS office, DMV office, local planning department, social security office. Distinct from GovernmentBuilding, which is the physical structure that may contain multiple offices.

Political Office Holder (Generic).label: AdministrativeArea
Political Office Holder (Generic).comment: An AdministrativeArea is a geographical region, typically governed by a specific authority. Also called political division, jurisdiction, governmental region, territory. Examples: A country, a state, a province, a city, a county.

Temperature.label: Energy
Temperature.comment: As a Quantity, Energy represents a numerical value combined with a unit of energy. Also called power, work, heat. Examples: "100 kWh", "500 Joules", "200 Calories", "1.21 Gigawatts".

Temperature.label: Mass
Temperature.comment: A quantity representing the amount of matter in an object, typically expressed with a unit of measure. Also called weight, bulk, quantity of matter. Examples: "5 kg", "10 pounds", "200 grams", "1 ton". Distinct from Quantity, which is a broader concept for any measurable amount.

Temperature.label: Distance
Temperature.comment: As a Quantity, Distance represents a numerical value combined with a unit of length. Also called length, extent, span, separation. Examples: "10 km", "5 miles", "300 meters", "2 feet".

Temperature.label: BodyMeasurementTypeEnumeration
Temperature.comment: A MeasurementTypeEnumeration listing various dimensions of a person's body, often used for clothing fit. Also called body dimension type, clothing size measurement, anthropometric measurement. Examples: "Chest circumference", "Waist size", "Inseam length", "Shoe size".

Temperature.label: MeasurementMethodEnum
Temperature.comment: An enumeration of methods used for measurement. Also called measurement technique, gauging method, assessment approach. Examples: "manual measurement", "automated sensor measurement", "self-reported measurement".

Person (Fan).label: Person
Person (Fan).comment: A Person is an individual human being, whether alive, dead, undead, or fictional. Also called individual, human, character. Examples: John Doe, Albert Einstein, Sherlock Holmes. Distinct from Organization, which is a group of people.

Person (Fan).label: Audience
Person (Fan).comment: An Audience is an Intangible entity representing the specific group of people for whom an item or creative work is intended. Also called target group, readership, viewership, demographic. Examples: children, teenagers, medical professionals, general public, investors.

Person (Fan).label: PeopleAudience

Also called demographic group, target audience, human audience. Examples: 'adults aged 18-35', 'students', 'retirees'. Distinct from Audience, which is a broader category including non-human audiences.

Person (Fan).label: Researcher
Person (Fan).comment: A Researcher is an Audience type representing individuals engaged in scientific or academic inquiry. Also called scientist, academic, scholar. Examples: a university professor, a lab scientist, a PhD student, an independent scholar.

Person (Fan).label: ParentAudience
Person (Fan).comment: A ParentAudience, as a PeopleAudience, describes characteristics of parents who might be interested in certain content. Also called parental demographic, parent group, family audience. Examples: 'parents of young children', 'parents of teenagers', 'expectant parents'. Distinct from PeopleAudience, which is a broader category for any group of people.

Duration.label: ServicePeriod

Cryptic Label.label: DDxElement

Cryptic Label.label: CategoryCode

Person (Designer).label: Menu

Person (Designer).label: Message
Person (Designer).comment: A creative work representing a single communication from a sender to one or more recipients. Also called communication, dispatch, note, email. Examples: an email, a text message, a direct message on social media, a voicemail.

Person (Sports Broadcaster).label: SportsEvent
Person (Sports Broadcaster).comment: An event involving athletic competition or display. Also called athletic contest, game, match, sporting competition. Examples: a football game, an Olympic event, a marathon race, a tennis tournament.

Person (Sports Broadcaster).label: BroadcastEvent

Person (Publicist).label: Role
Person (Publicist).comment: Additional information describing a relationship or property, such as a person's function in an organization or a character played in a movie. Person (Publicist).label: Notary
Person (Publicist).comment: A Notary is a local business or individual providing legal services, specifically witnessing and authenticating signatures on documents. Also called notary public, public notary, legal witness. Examples: a notary service at a bank, an independent notary, a legal office offering notarization. Distinct from Lawyer, who provides broader legal counsel.

Person (Publicist).label: Brand
Person (Publicist).comment: A Brand is an Intangible entity representing a name, symbol, or design used by an organization to identify and distinguish its products or services. Also called product line, trademark, label, marque. Examples: Nike, Apple, Coca-Cola, Google.

Person (Actor).label: Person
Person (Actor).comment: A Person is an individual human being, whether alive, dead, undead, or fictional. Also called individual, human, character. Examples: John Doe, Albert Einstein, Sherlock Holmes. Distinct from Organization, which is a group of people.

Person (Actor).label: PerformanceRole
Person (Actor).comment: A PerformanceRole, as a Role, is a role an entity plays in a theatrical performance, such as a movie or TV series. Also called acting role, character role, stage role. Examples: 'actor in a film', 'director of a play', 'musician in a concert'. Distinct from OrganizationRole, which is a role within an organization.

Person (Actor).label: Play
Person (Actor).comment: A Play is a CreativeWork in the form of literature, primarily consisting of dialogue between characters, intended for theatrical performance. Also called stage play, drama, theatrical work. Examples: "Hamlet", "Death of a Salesman", "Hamilton", "A Streetcar Named Desire". Distinct from TheaterEvent, which is the actual performance of a play.

Person (Actor).label: TheaterEvent
Person (Actor).comment: An event representing a live performance in a theater. Also called stage play, theatrical show, drama performance. Examples: a Broadway musical, a local community play, a Shakespearean tragedy.

Person (Actor).label: PerformAction
Person (Actor).comment: A PerformAction, as a PlayAction, is the act of participating in performance arts. Also called act, perform, stage. Person (Model).label: Person

Person (Model).label: ProductModel
Person (Model).comment: A ProductModel is a Product representing a datasheet or vendor specification of a prototypical product description. Examples: the technical specifications for a new laptop model, a design document for a car engine, a vendor's product data sheet, a conceptual product design.

Person (Model).label: ClothingStore
Person (Model).comment: A local business specializing in the retail sale of apparel and accessories. Also called apparel store, boutique, fashion shop, garment retailer. Examples: H&M, Zara, Nordstrom, a local boutique. Distinct from Store, which is a general retail establishment.

Person (Model).label: Product
Person (Model).comment: A Product is any offered good or service. Also called item, merchandise, offering. Examples: a pair of shoes, a concert ticket, a car rental service, an episode of a TV show.

Person (Model).label: Vehicle

Group of People (Social Circle).label: Organization
Group of People (Social Circle).comment: An Organization is a group of people with a particular purpose, such as a school, NGO, corporation, or club. Also called entity, institution, association. Examples: Google, Harvard University, Red Cross, a local sports club. Distinct from Person, which is an individual.

Group of People (Social Circle).label: DanceGroup
Group of People (Social Circle).comment: A DanceGroup is a performing organization specializing in dance, often presenting choreographed performances. Also called dance company, ballet troupe, dance ensemble, dance collective. Examples: Alvin Ailey American Dance Theater, Riverdance, New York City Ballet, Bolshoi Ballet.

Group of People (Social Circle).label: Cooperative
Group of People (Social Circle).comment: A Cooperative is an organization formed as a joint project by multiple organizations or individuals, often for mutual benefit. Also called member-owned business, co-op, collective. Examples: REI (Recreational Equipment, Inc.), Ocean Spray, Sunkist Growers, credit unions. Distinct from Corporation, which is a business entity owned by shareholders.

Group of People (Social Circle).label: PerformingGroup
Group of People (Social Circle).comment: A PerformingGroup is an organization of performers, such as a band, orchestra, or circus. Also called performance ensemble, troupe, artistic group. Examples: Cirque du Soleil, a local theatre company, a dance troupe. Distinct from MusicGroup, which is specifically for musical performers.

Group of People (Social Circle).label: SocialEvent

Person (Pop Star/Actress).label: MusicEvent

Person (Pop Star/Actress).label: PeopleAudience
Person (Pop Star/Actress).comment: A PeopleAudience, as an Audience, describes a set of characteristics belonging to people, e.g., who compose an item's target audience. Distinct from Audience, which is a broader category including non-human audiences.

Person (Pop Star/Actress).label: MusicVideoObject
Person (Pop Star/Actress).comment: A MusicVideoObject, as a MediaObject, is a video file primarily featuring a musical performance or accompanying a song. Also called music video, song video, official video. Examples: 'Thriller' music video by Michael Jackson, a Vevo music video, a live performance video. Distinct from MovieClip, which is a segment of a film.

Social Media Platform.label: SocialMediaPosting
Social Media Platform.comment: A creative work published on a social media platform, such as a blog post, tweet, or Facebook update. Also called social post, microblog post, status update, online share. Examples: a tweet from a celebrity, a Facebook status update, a blog post on Medium, an Instagram caption.

Social Media Platform.label: DiscussionForumPosting
Social Media Platform.comment: A social media posting that is an entry or message within an online discussion forum. Also called Forum post, message board entry, thread reply, online discussion. Social Media Platform.label: DigitalPlatformEnumeration
Social Media Platform.comment: An enumeration listing common technology platforms, used to specify where an action or content is available. Also called Technology platform, software platform, operating system, device type. Examples: iOS, Android, Web, Desktop, Console. Social Media Platform.label: BlogPosting
Social Media Platform.comment: An Article that is an individual entry or post published within a blog. Also called blog post, blog entry, weblog post. Social Media Platform.label: SocialEvent

TV Series.label: TVEpisode

TV Series.label: TVSeason

TV Series.label: TVSeries

TV Series.label: Episode

TV Series.label: Series

University.label: CollegeOrUniversity
University.comment: A third-level educational institution providing higher education. Also called university, college, higher education institution. Examples: Harvard University, Oxford College, Massachusetts Institute of Technology, Sorbonne University. Distinct from EducationalOrganization, which is a broader category for any educational body.

University.label: ResearchOrganization
University.comment: A ResearchOrganization is an Organization dedicated to conducting research. Also called scientific institute, research company, academic research center. Examples: Max Planck Society, Bell Labs, a university research department, a pharmaceutical research firm.

University.label: School
University.comment: An educational organization providing instruction to students, typically for primary or secondary education. Also called educational institution, academy, learning center, college. Examples: a public elementary school, a private high school, a vocational school, a university.

University.label: ResearchProject
University.comment: A ResearchProject is a Project representing a planned enterprise aimed at scientific or academic inquiry. Also called research initiative, study, academic project. Examples: a clinical trial, a grant-funded scientific study, a historical research project, a university-led exploration.

University.label: EducationalOrganization
University.comment: An EducationalOrganization is a CivicStructure that provides education. Also called learning institution, academic body, school. Examples: A university, a high school, a vocational college, a research institute.

Person (Student).label: Person
Person (Student).comment: A Person is an individual human being, whether alive, dead, undead, or fictional. Also called individual, human, character. Examples: John Doe, Albert Einstein, Sherlock Holmes. Distinct from Organization, which is a group of people.

Person (Student).label: Course
Person (Student).comment: A Course is a description of an educational program or curriculum designed to impart knowledge, competence, or ability to learners. Also called educational program, curriculum, study program, academic course. Examples: "Introduction to Python Programming," "Art History 101," "Advanced Calculus," "Yoga Teacher Training." Distinct from CourseInstance, which is a specific offering of a course at a particular time and place.

Person (Student).label: School
Person (Student).comment: An educational organization providing instruction to students, typically for primary or secondary education. Also called educational institution, academy, learning center, college. Examples: a public elementary school, a private high school, a vocational school, a university.

Person (Student).label: Residence
Person (Student).comment: A Residence is a Place where a person lives. Also called home, dwelling, abode. Examples: a house, an apartment, a condominium, a dormitory room.

Person (Student).label: CourseInstance
Person (Student).comment: A CourseInstance is a specific offering of an educational course, distinguished by its particular time, location, medium, or target student group. Also called course section, class session, course offering, specific class. Examples: "Fall 2023 Introduction to Python (Online)," "Spring 2024 Art History 101 (Campus A, Section B)," "Summer Intensive Yoga Teacher Training." Distinct from Course, which is the general description of the educational content.

Age.label: Number
Age.comment: Number is a data type representing numerical values. Also called numeric value, quantity, digit. Examples: 10, 3.14, -5, 1000000. Distinct from Text, which represents character strings.

Age.label: AdultOrientedEnumeration
Age.comment: AdultOrientedEnumeration is an Enumeration of factors that make a product or content relevant or potentially restricted for adults only. Also called adult content classification, age restriction type, mature content indicator. Examples: `AdultSexualContent`, `ViolentContent`, `GamblingContent`.

Age.label: Integer
Age.comment: Integer is a data type representing a whole number without a fractional component. Also called whole number, natural number (if positive), counting number. Examples: 0, 1, -5, 1000. Distinct from Float, which includes decimal values.

Age.label: Duration
Age.comment: As a Quantity, Duration represents a period of time, typically expressed in ISO 8601 format. Also called time span, period, length of time. Examples: "PT1H30M" (1 hour 30 minutes), "P3D" (3 days), "PT2H" (2 hours).

Age.label: MonetaryAmount
Age.comment: A structured value representing a monetary value or range, typically expressed with a currency. Also called amount of money, financial value, currency amount. Examples: "$50 USD", "£1,000 to £1,000,000 GBP", "€25.99". Distinct from PriceSpecification, which describes the price of an offer.

Person (Tourist).label: TouristTrip
Person (Tourist).comment: An itinerary or journey undertaken by visitors for tourism purposes, often involving visits to multiple places of interest. Also called vacation itinerary, travel plan, sightseeing tour. Examples: a two-week European tour, a weekend getaway to a national park, a cruise itinerary.

Person (Tourist).label: TouristDestination
Person (Tourist).comment: A place, region, or area that is a primary focus for tourism, often containing multiple tourist attractions. Also called travel destination, vacation spot, tourist region. Examples: Paris, the Grand Canyon, the Caribbean islands, a specific resort town. Distinct from TouristAttraction, which is a specific point of interest within a destination.

Person (Tourist).label: Person
Person (Tourist).comment: A Person is an individual human being, whether alive, dead, undead, or fictional. Also called individual, human, character. Examples: John Doe, Albert Einstein, Sherlock Holmes. Distinct from Organization, which is a group of people.

Person (Tourist).label: TouristAttraction
Person (Tourist).comment: A specific place or feature that draws tourists due to its interest or appeal. Also called point of interest, visitor attraction, landmark. Examples: the Eiffel Tower, a national park, a historical museum, a famous statue. Distinct from TouristDestination, which is a broader area containing one or more attractions.

Person (Tourist).label: Trip
Person (Tourist).comment: A general term for a journey or itinerary involving visits to one or more places. Also called journey, travel, excursion. Examples: a business trip, a family vacation, a day trip to the beach.

Web Link.label: URL
Web Link.comment: A data type representing a Uniform Resource Locator, which specifies the address of a resource on the internet. Also called web address, link, internet address. Examples: "https://schema.org", "ftp://example.com/file.zip", "mailto:info@example.com".

Web Link.label: LinkRole
Web Link.comment: A LinkRole is an intangible role representing a Web link, allowing for the specification of link relationships and other HTML link element details outside of HTML. Also called URL role, hyperlink descriptor, web link attribute. Examples: a link with 'linkRelationship' 'amphtml', a canonical URL link, a link to a related resource.

Web Link.label: WebPage
Web Link.comment: A single document or resource accessible via a web browser, typically part of a larger website. Also called web document, HTML page, internet page. Examples: a product page on an e-commerce site, a news article page, a contact us page.

Web Link.label: WebSite
Web Link.comment: A collection of related web pages and other items, typically served from a single domain. Also called website, internet site, web presence. Examples: schema.org, Wikipedia, The New York Times website.

Web Link.label: WebContent
Web Link.comment: A general type representing any content accessible via the web, including web pages, websites, and their elements. Also called web content item, online content, digital web asset. Examples: a blog post, an entire website, an image embedded on a page.

Form (Document Type).label: CDCPMDRecord
Form (Document Type).comment: A CDCPMDRecord is a StructuredValue representing a record in the CDC tabular data format used for hospital data reporting, specifically for COVID-19 related data. Also called CDC hospital data record, COVID-19 data record. Examples: a daily hospital bed occupancy report, a weekly ICU patient count record.

Form (Document Type).label: StructuredValue
Form (Document Type).comment: A value for a property that has a complex internal structure rather than being a simple text or reference. Also called complex data type, composite value, structured data. Examples: an address object with street, city, and zip code; a price specification with amount and currency; a time range with start and end times.

Form (Document Type).label: TypeAndQuantityNode
Form (Document Type).comment: A structured value indicating the quantity, unit of measurement, and business function of goods within a bundle offer. Also called quantity specification, offer item details, bundle component. Examples: "3 kg of apples for sale", "2 units of product X as a bonus", "1 liter of milk in a grocery bundle".

Form (Document Type).label: Thing
Form (Document Type).comment: The most generic and fundamental type in schema.org, representing any item or entity. Also called entity, item, object. Examples: a person, a book, a place, an event.

Form (Document Type).label: DataType
Form (Document Type).comment: DataType is a fundamental classification for the kind of values that can be stored or manipulated, such as numbers, text, or booleans. Also called primitive type, data format, value type. Examples: Integer, String, Boolean, Float, Date.

Person (Journalist).label: Person
Person (Journalist).comment: A Person is an individual human being, whether alive, dead, undead, or fictional. Also called individual, human, character. Examples: John Doe, Albert Einstein, Sherlock Holmes. Distinct from Organization, which is a group of people.

Person (Journalist).label: NewsArticle
Person (Journalist).comment: A NewsArticle, as an Article, is a creative work whose content reports news or provides background context for understanding news. Also called news report, news story, journalistic article. Examples: a breaking news report, an investigative journalism piece, an opinion column in a newspaper. Distinct from BlogPosting, which is typically less formal and often personal.

Person (Journalist).label: ReportageNewsArticle
Person (Journalist).comment: A ReportageNewsArticle is a NewsArticle representing news articles based on factual journalistic reporting, emphasizing verified information and multiple viewpoints. Also called news report, journalistic article, factual news. Examples: a breaking news story about a political event, an investigative report on a social issue, a factual account of a natural disaster, a report on scientific findings. Distinct from AnalysisNewsArticle, which goes deeper into analysis.

Person (Journalist).label: Article
Person (Journalist).comment: An Article is a CreativeWork, typically a written piece such as a news report, magazine feature, or investigative report. Also called written piece, report, feature, essay, column. Examples: a newspaper article about local politics, a magazine feature on travel, a scientific journal article, a blog post. Distinct from BlogPosting, which is a specific type of article published on a blog.

Person (Journalist).label: Report
Person (Journalist).comment: A Report is an Article generated by a governmental or non-governmental organization. Also called official report, document, publication. Examples: an annual financial report, a government research report, a UN policy report, a company's sustainability report.

Descriptive Title for Musician.label: MusicAlbumProductionType
Descriptive Title for Musician.comment: MusicAlbumProductionType is an enumeration classifying a music album by its content type. Also called album type, production category. Examples: StudioAlbum, LiveAlbum, Soundtrack, CompilationAlbum. Distinct from MusicAlbumReleaseType, which describes the release format.

Descriptive Title for Musician.label: MusicEvent
Descriptive Title for Musician.comment: A MusicEvent is an event primarily featuring musical performances. Also called concert, musical performance, gig. Examples: a rock concert, a classical symphony performance, a music festival. Distinct from PerformingArtsEvent, which includes broader performance types like theatre or dance.

Descriptive Title for Musician.label: MusicRecording
Descriptive Title for Musician.comment: A MusicRecording, as a CreativeWork, is a recorded performance of a musical composition, usually a single song. Also called music track, song recording, audio track. Examples: 'Yesterday' by The Beatles (the recorded version), a single from an album, a demo track. Distinct from MusicComposition, which is the abstract musical work.

Descriptive Title for Musician.label: MusicGroup
Descriptive Title for Musician.comment: A MusicGroup, as a PerformingGroup, is an organization of musicians, such as a band or orchestra, or a solo musician. Also called band, musical ensemble, orchestra, solo artist. Examples: The Beatles, New York Philharmonic, Taylor Swift. Distinct from PerformingGroup, which is a broader category for any performance group.

Descriptive Title for Musician.label: MusicComposition
Descriptive Title for Musician.comment: A MusicComposition is a musical work, such as a song or symphony, that can be performed or recorded. Also called musical piece, song, score. Examples: Beethoven's 5th Symphony, 'Bohemian Rhapsody' by Queen, a jingle. Distinct from MusicRecording, which is a recorded performance of a composition.

Quantity (Shows).label: Quantity
Quantity (Shows).comment: Quantity is a data type representing measurable amounts such as distance, time, mass, or weight. Also called amount, measure, magnitude. Examples: '3 kg', '4 milligrams', '10 meters', '2 hours'.

Quantity (Shows).label: Mass
Quantity (Shows).comment: A quantity representing the amount of matter in an object, typically expressed with a unit of measure. Also called weight, bulk, quantity of matter. Examples: "5 kg", "10 pounds", "200 grams", "1 ton". Distinct from Quantity, which is a broader concept for any measurable amount.

Quantity (Shows).label: Number
Quantity (Shows).comment: Number is a data type representing numerical values. Also called numeric value, quantity, digit. Examples: 10, 3.14, -5, 1000000. Distinct from Text, which represents character strings.

Quantity (Shows).label: Duration
Quantity (Shows).comment: As a Quantity, Duration represents a period of time, typically expressed in ISO 8601 format. Also called time span, period, length of time. Examples: "PT1H30M" (1 hour 30 minutes), "P3D" (3 days), "PT2H" (2 hours).

Quantity (Shows).label: TVSeason
Quantity (Shows).comment: A distinct period of a television series, comprising multiple episodes, dedicated to TV broadcast and associated online delivery. Also called television season, broadcast season, show season. Examples: 'Season 1 of The Crown', 'The final season of Breaking Bad'. Distinct from Season, which is a more general media season.

Group of People (Audience).label: Audience
Group of People (Audience).comment: An Audience is an Intangible entity representing the specific group of people for whom an item or creative work is intended. Also called target group, readership, viewership, demographic. Examples: children, teenagers, medical professionals, general public, investors.

Group of People (Audience).label: PeopleAudience
Group of People (Audience).comment: A PeopleAudience, as an Audience, describes a set of characteristics belonging to people, e.g., who compose an item's target audience. Also called demographic group, target audience, human audience. Examples: 'adults aged 18-35', 'students', 'retirees'. Distinct from Audience, which is a broader category including non-human audiences.

Group of People (Audience).label: Event
Group of People (Audience).comment: An Event is a Thing happening at a specific time and location, such as a concert, lecture, or festival. Also called happening, occurrence, occasion. Examples: A rock concert, a public lecture, a sports match, a community festival.

Group of People (Audience).label: PerformingGroup
Group of People (Audience).comment: A PerformingGroup is an organization of performers, such as a band, orchestra, or circus. Also called performance ensemble, troupe, artistic group. Examples: Cirque du Soleil, a local theatre company, a dance troupe. Distinct from MusicGroup, which is specifically for musical performers.

Group of People (Audience).label: EducationalAudience
Group of People (Audience).comment: An EducationalAudience is an Audience specifically targeted for educational content or programs. Also called student group, learner demographic, academic audience. Examples: K-12 students, university undergraduates, adult learners, professional development participants.

Song Title.label: SheetMusic
Song Title.comment: Printed or written musical notation, as distinct from a performance or recording. Also called musical score, notation, music manuscript, song sheet. Examples: a piano concerto score, guitar tablature, a vocal sheet for a song, an orchestral score.

Song Title.label: MusicComposition
Song Title.comment: A MusicComposition is a musical work, such as a song or symphony, that can be performed or recorded. Also called musical piece, song, score. Examples: Beethoven's 5th Symphony, 'Bohemian Rhapsody' by Queen, a jingle. Distinct from MusicRecording, which is a recorded performance of a composition.

Song Title.label: MusicAlbum
Song Title.comment: A MusicAlbum, as a MusicPlaylist, is a collection of music tracks released together. Also called album, record album, studio album. Examples: 'Thriller' by Michael Jackson, 'Abbey Road' by The Beatles, a compilation album. Distinct from MusicRecording, which is usually a single song.

Song Title.label: MusicRecording
Song Title.comment: A MusicRecording, as a CreativeWork, is a recorded performance of a musical composition, usually a single song. Also called music track, song recording, audio track. Examples: 'Yesterday' by The Beatles (the recorded version), a single from an album, a demo track. Distinct from MusicComposition, which is the abstract musical work.

Song Title.label: MusicPlaylist
Song Title.comment: A MusicPlaylist, as a CreativeWork, is an ordered collection of music tracks. Also called playlist, music compilation, track list. Examples: a Spotify playlist, a radio station's daily playlist, a custom mix CD. Distinct from MusicAlbum, which is a formally released collection of tracks.

Quantity (People).label: Quantity
Quantity (People).comment: Quantity is a data type representing measurable amounts such as distance, time, mass, or weight. Also called amount, measure, magnitude. Examples: '3 kg', '4 milligrams', '10 meters', '2 hours'.

Quantity (People).label: Mass
Quantity (People).comment: A quantity representing the amount of matter in an object, typically expressed with a unit of measure. Also called weight, bulk, quantity of matter. Examples: "5 kg", "10 pounds", "200 grams", "1 ton". Distinct from Quantity, which is a broader concept for any measurable amount.

Quantity (People).label: StatisticalPopulation
Quantity (People).comment: A set of instances of a given type that satisfy specific constraints, used for statistical analysis. Also called statistical group, data population, sample group, target demographic. Examples: all persons with a home location in a specific city, all events occurring in a particular year, all news articles mentioning a certain keyword. Distinct from StatisticalVariable, which represents a measurable metric within a population.

Quantity (People).label: Number
Quantity (People).comment: Number is a data type representing numerical values. Also called numeric value, quantity, digit. Examples: 10, 3.14, -5, 1000000. Distinct from Text, which represents character strings.

Quantity (People).label: Distance
Quantity (People).comment: As a Quantity, Distance represents a numerical value combined with a unit of length. Also called length, extent, span, separation. Examples: "10 km", "5 miles", "300 meters", "2 feet".

Aircraft Model.label: Flight
Aircraft Model.comment: A Flight is a Trip representing an airline journey. Also called air travel, plane ride, air route. Examples: Flight BA249 from London to Rio, a domestic flight from New York to Chicago, a charter flight.

Aircraft Model.label: Airline
Aircraft Model.comment: An Airline is an Organization that provides air transportation services for passengers. Also called air carrier, air transport company, flight operator. Examples: United Airlines, British Airways, Lufthansa, Southwest Airlines. Distinct from Airport, which is the facility where planes take off and land.

Aircraft Model.label: Car
Aircraft Model.comment: A wheeled, self-powered motor vehicle primarily used for personal transportation. Also called automobile, motorcar, auto, vehicle. Examples: Toyota Camry, Ford F-150, Tesla Model 3, Honda Civic.

Aircraft Model.label: Vehicle
Aircraft Model.comment: A device designed or used for transporting people or cargo across various environments. Also called conveyance, transport, automobile. Examples: a car, a bicycle, an airplane, a boat, a truck.

Aircraft Model.label: ProductModel
Aircraft Model.comment: A ProductModel is a Product representing a datasheet or vendor specification of a prototypical product description. Also called product prototype, product specification, product blueprint. Examples: the technical specifications for a new laptop model, a design document for a car engine, a vendor's product data sheet, a conceptual product design.

Emergency Service Organization.label: EmergencyService
Emergency Service Organization.comment: An EmergencyService is a LocalBusiness providing immediate assistance in urgent situations. Also called emergency response, crisis service. Examples: A fire station, an emergency room, a police department, an ambulance service.

Emergency Service Organization.label: SearchRescueOrganization
Emergency Service Organization.comment: An organization dedicated to finding and providing aid to people who are lost or in imminent danger. Also called SAR team, rescue service, emergency search unit. Examples: a mountain rescue team, a coast guard search and rescue unit, a volunteer SAR group.

Emergency Service Organization.label: Organization
Emergency Service Organization.comment: An Organization is a group of people with a particular purpose, such as a school, NGO, corporation, or club. Also called entity, institution, association. Examples: Google, Harvard University, Red Cross, a local sports club. Distinct from Person, which is an individual.

Emergency Service Organization.label: MedicalOrganization
Emergency Service Organization.comment: An organization, physical or virtual, operating in the medical domain, such as a hospital or clinic. Also called healthcare organization, medical institution, health system. Examples: "Mayo Clinic", "World Health Organization", "Doctors Without Borders". Distinct from Organization, which is a broader category for any group.

Emergency Service Organization.label: Airline
Emergency Service Organization.comment: An Airline is an Organization that provides air transportation services for passengers. Also called air carrier, air transport company, flight operator. Examples: United Airlines, British Airways, Lufthansa, Southwest Airlines. Distinct from Airport, which is the facility where planes take off and land.

Year.label: Date
Year.comment: Date is a data type representing a specific calendar date, typically formatted according to ISO 8601. Also called calendar date, specific day. Examples: "2023-10-27", "1999-12-31", "0001-01-01".

Year.label: Season
Year.comment: A distinct period within a media series, such as a television show, radio program, or video game. Also called media season, series installment, broadcast season. Examples: 'Season 1 of Game of Thrones', 'The Fall 2023 radio season', 'Chapter 3 of a video game series'. Distinct from TVSeason, which is specifically for television broadcasts.

Year.label: Schedule
Year.comment: A definition of a repeating time period used to describe a regularly occurring event, specifying frequency, days, and start/end times. Also called timetable, recurring event plan, calendar entry, routine. Examples: a weekly yoga class schedule, a bus route timetable, a daily meeting schedule, a concert series calendar.

Year.label: Event
Year.comment: An Event is a Thing happening at a specific time and location, such as a concert, lecture, or festival. Also called happening, occurrence, occasion. Examples: A rock concert, a public lecture, a sports match, a community festival.

Year.label: DayOfWeek
Year.comment: An enumeration representing a specific day of the week, used for scheduling or recurring events. Also called Weekday, calendar day, day name. Examples: Monday, Tuesday, Saturday, Sunday. Distinct from Date, which specifies a particular calendar date.
